## CMV POLYRADICULOPATHY
Infection in immunocompetent patients is rare and usually associated with
minimal or no symptoms. Patients in whom the risk for CMV disease is increased
include solid organ and bone marrow transplant recipients, persons receiving
prolonged immunosuppressive chemotherapy, and persons with advanced HIV disease
indicated by a CD4 count of less than 50 cells/microliter. Treatment is complex
and requires Infectious Diseases consultation.
## Duration of antimicrobial therapy
Duration is likely to be prolonged and is individualized based on response.
Patients may be converted to oral therapy after initial intravenous therapy and
after clinical improvement of severe disease.
## Treatment of mild to moderate disease or following clinical improvement of
## severe disease
## Inpatient

Valganciclovir 900 mg PO q12h ($$$) [R,O]
## Treatment of severe disease
Ganciclovir 5 mg/kg IV q12h ($$$$) [R,O]
< OR >
Foscarnet 90 mg/kg IV q12h ($$$$) [R,O]
## Outpatient

Valganciclovir 900 mg PO BID ($$$) [R,O]
Non-VA order for above
## Treatment of severe disease
Refer to Inpatient Antimicrobial CDSS. References:
Guidelines for Prevention and Treatment of Opportunistic Infections in HIV
Infected Adults and Adolescents. AIDSinfo (2015) 1-282
